brief: Goldman Sachs Prime Services' monthly hedge fund letter summary for August 2026, based on 438 client letters. Global equities recovered from July's reversal, with the S&P 500 near all-time highs on strong earnings, notably software results offsetting AI concerns. The 30-year Treasury yield hit its highest level in almost twenty years on fiscal concerns and corporate borrowing, before Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's mid-month buyback announcement temporarily pushed yields down and lifted gold. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish address raised rate-hike expectations, while restricted oil supply and growing AI-capex/data-center spending kept inflation and geopolitical concerns elevated. Hedge funds returned 0.9% in August on a strategy-weighted basis. Equity long/short gains were modest and beta-driven, with generalists beating sector specialists. Systematic macro/CTA was the top-performing strategy in August and remains the second-best performer year-to-date, on energy, metals, agricultural and equity-market trends. Quant posted one of its best months of the year so far despite a momentum-driven mid-month regional sell-off that produced its worst single day in over two years. Long-biased and pension-allocated funds led their respective breakdowns.

cards.claim: Systematic macro/CTA was the top-performing hedge fund strategy in August 2026 and remains the second-best performing strategy year-to-date, with trends in energy, metals, agricultural, and equity markets driving returns.
cards.anchor: Systematic macro / CTA was once again the top-performing strategy – and remains the second-best performing strategy this year – with trends in energy, metals, agricultural, and equity markets driving returns.

cards.claim: Quant strategies posted one of their best monthly returns of 2026 so far in August, despite a mid-month momentum-driven regional sell-off that produced their worst single day of performance in over two years.
cards.anchor: Quant strategies also posted one of their best monthly returns for the year so far, despite a mid-month sell-off across regions driven by momentum, resulting in their worst day of performance in over two years.
